fullPassage: What do you think good design is? Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative. There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible. All of these are important elements of design. However, there is a new idea called “universal design.” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions. Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers. Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services. Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product. Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use. The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities. If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want. If desired, the user can work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height. Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts, automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems. Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design. A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands. Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language. For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor. As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc. Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With universal design, no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal design suggest that it should be part of every design. Take a look around you. Is there anything that needs improvement so that it can be accessible to more people? If so, why not create a design and bring joy to more people?

questions.passage: A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands.  Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities.  Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities.  Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues.  For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language.  For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements.  In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 정보 전달과 접근성.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문 'braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor'와 일치 ←정답

❌ ② 본문 'Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues'에서 문자 언어'만이 아니라'고 했으므로 '오직 문자 언어만'은 불일치

❌ ③ 본문 'A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand'에서 팔꿈치나 쥔 손으로 '열 수 있다'고 했으므로 불일치

❌ ④ 본문 'finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the ~ restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language'에서 기호를 찾는 편이 '더 쉽다'고 했으므로 불일치
det.tip: 점자=층 선택 도움(일치). 나머지는 본문과 반대로 뒤집은 함정입니다.

ch: 점자는 층 번호를 나타내어 시각 장애인이 원하는 층을 고르도록 돕는다.
정보는 오직 문자 언어를 통해서만 전달되어야 한다.
레버형 손잡이가 달린 문은 팔꿈치나 쥔 주먹으로는 열 수 없다.
외국인 여행자는 화장실 기호보다 현지 언어를 해석하는 편이 더 쉽다.

questions.passage: They are all ①<u>designed</u> for left-handed people.  Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use.  The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities.  If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they ②<u>wants</u>.  If desired, the user can work while ③<u>standing</u>.  A wheelchair user is also ④<u>able</u> to use the desk at a comfortable height.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② wants → want: 관계절의 주어 they가 복수이므로 복수 동사 want
det.analysis:
① designed: 'They are all designed for left-handed people'에서 제품이 '설계된' 것이라 수동태 과거분사 designed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② wants → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'the users can adjust it to the heights they ___'에서 관계절의 주어는 they(복수)예요. 그래서 복수 동사 want로 써야 해요. wants(단수)로 쓰면 they와 수가 안 맞아 틀려요. ❌ wants는 틀림 ←정답

③ standing: 'the user can work while standing'에서 접속사 while 뒤에 분사 standing이 온 것으로, '서 있는 동안(서서)'이라는 뜻이라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ able: 'A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk'에서 'be able to(~할 수 있다)' 구문이라 able이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 복수 주어 they + 복수 동사 want: 주어-동사 수 일치

questions.passage: Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities.  Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities.  Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues.  For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language.  For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements.  In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 유니버설 디자인은 정보를 전달할 때 문자 언어와 '보편적 기호(universal symbols)' 외에 무엇을 함께 활용해야 한다고 했는지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 정보 전달의 세 번째 수단.
det.analysis: 본문 'Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues.'에서 정보는 문자 언어와 보편적 기호뿐 아니라 '소리 신호(audio cues)'로도 전달되어야 한다고 했다. 따라서 빈자리에 들어갈 답은 audio cues다.
det.tip: not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues에서 audio cues를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments.  Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed.  A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design.  A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands.  Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities.  Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 레버형 문손잡이는 꽉 쥐는 것(firm grip) 외에 어떤 동작도 필요하지 않다고 했는지, 그 동작을 나타내는 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 레버형 손잡이가 요구하지 않는 동작.
det.analysis: 본문 'A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example ~'에서 레버형 손잡이는 '꽉 쥐는 것(firm grip)'이나 '비트는 것(twisting)'이 필요 없다고 했다. firm grip 외에 언급된 동작은 twisting이다.
det.tip: requires no firm grip or twisting(꽉 쥐거나 비틀 필요가 없다)에서 twisting을 찾습니다.

questions.passage: A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened __________ (use) an elbow or a closed hand. This benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: using (분사구문).
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'can be opened ___ an elbow or a closed hand'에서 빈칸은 '팔꿈치나 쥔 손을 사용해서'라는 뜻으로 앞 문장에 이어지는 분사구문 자리다. 분사구문은 동사를 -ing 형태로 쓰므로 use를 using으로 바꿔야 한다. '(by) using an elbow(팔꿈치를 사용하여)'로 해석된다.
det.tip: 동작 수단을 나타내는 분사구문: opened using an elbow(팔꿈치를 사용하여 열리는)

questions.passage: What do you think good design is?  Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative.  There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible.  All of these are important elements of design.  However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.  Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 아우르는 중심 소재.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 유니버설 디자인이 유연성·접근성·낮은 신체적 노력·정보 전달 등을 통해 다양한 사람이 장벽 없이 쓸 수 있게 한다는 것이 글 전체의 주제 ← 정답

❌ ② 왼손잡이용 제품은 하나의 예시일 뿐 판매 전략이 주제가 아님

❌ ③ 자동문 비용·관리는 본문에 없는 내용

❌ ④ 왼손잡이 비율의 시대별 변화는 다루지 않음
det.tip: 유연성·접근성·낮은 노력·정보 전달을 관통하는 것이 유니버설 디자인입니다.

ch: 다양한 사용자의 요구를 반영해 모두가 장벽 없이 접근·사용하게 하는 유니버설 디자인
왼손잡이용 가위와 컴퓨터 마우스를 판매하기 위한 구체적인 마케팅 전략
공공건물에 자동문을 설치할 때 드는 비용과 유지·관리 방법
전 세계 인구 중 왼손잡이가 차지하는 비율이 시대별로 변화해 온 과정

questions.passage: What do you think good design is?  Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative.  There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible.  All of these are important elements of design.  However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.  Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글쓴이가 전하려는 핵심 메시지.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문은 유니버설 디자인이 '모두'에게 이롭다고 하므로 '특정 장애인만을 위한' 것은 반대

❌ ② 본문 'design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions'에서 겉모습만으로는 충분하지 않다고 했으므로 반대

✅ ③ 본문 'Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With universal design, no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort.'와 통하는 핵심 메시지 ← 정답

❌ ④ 제작 비용을 낮추는 것이 가장 중요하다는 내용은 본문에 없음
det.tip: 모두에게 이롭고 누구도 불편을 견딜 필요가 없게 하는 것이 요지입니다.

ch: 유니버설 디자인은 특정 장애인만을 위해 만들어진 특별한 설계 방식이다.
잘 만든 디자인은 겉모습이 아름답기만 하면 충분하다.
유니버설 디자인은 모두가 불편 없이 접근하고 사용할 수 있게 하는 것을 지향한다.
디자인에서 가장 중요한 것은 언제나 제작 비용을 낮추는 일이다.

questions.passage: Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor.  As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc.  Universal design is beneficial to everyone.  With universal design, __________.  The supporters of universal design suggest that it should be part of every design.  Take a look around you.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"누구도 불필요한 불편을 참고 견딜 필요가 없다." (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) discomfort, needs, no, one, put, to, unnecessary, up, with 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort
det.analysis:
'누구도 ~할 필요가 없다'는 'No one needs to + 동사원형'으로 시작해요: no + one + needs + to.

'참고 견디다'는 'put up with'라는 굳어진 표현이에요. 세 단어가 한 덩어리로 움직여요: put + up + with.

무엇을 견디는가 하면 '불필요한 불편'이에요. 형용사가 명사 앞에 오므로 unnecessary discomfort로 써요: unnecessary + discomfort.

순서대로 이으면 no / one / needs / to / put / up / with / unnecessary / discomfort.
det.tip: No one needs to(누구도 ~할 필요가 없다) + put up with(~을 참고 견디다) + unnecessary discomfort(불필요한 불편)

questions.wa: no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort
accept: no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort
